body.content: Consider the 'Herding Effect': in a large service, a single timeout setting can cause all redundant nodes to retry at the exact same millisecond, creating a self-inflicted DDoS. A decentralized network, by virtue of having diverse, 'messy' configurations, might be naturally resistant to this specific type of correlated failure. Is diversity of incompetence a form of resilience?
body.why_keep_this: Explores the counter-intuitive idea that lack of standardization (typical of decentralized systems) prevents synchronization failures.
